newsitem.title: NORWAY: Christiania shareholders say yes to Storebrand ST.
newsitem.headline: Christiania shareholders say yes to Storebrand ST.

text.p: A majority of shareholders in Norway's second largest bank, Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA, gave the green light on Thursday to a proposed merger with the country's largest insurance group Storebrand ASA.
The fusion was passed at an extraordinary general meeting and brings the formation of the proposed Christiania Group a step closer.
Storebrand's shareholders are due to gather to debate and vote on the merger at 1600 GMT. The result of that vote hangs on a knife edge and market sources say it could go either way.
Christiania said 389,947,000 shares, or 99,86 percent of the shares represented at the extraordinary meeting, voted in favour of the merger with 556,900 against.
"Leading Norwegian and foreign investors voted yes and that indicates there will be a number of yes votes at Storebrand too," Tom Ruud, CEO in Christiania Bank, told Reuters.
If the plan goes ahead, it will form Norway's largest financial group and the sixth biggest in the Nordic region.

On Monday, the Finance Ministry, as the largest shareholder in Christiania Bank, said it would support the plans. The state owns just over 50 percent of the bank's equity after the government bailed out many of the country's banks following a financial crisis between 1988 and 1992.
